sections.h2: What should a Farmington Hills homeowner know before selling quickly?
sections.html:
Farmington Hills is a large Oakland County suburb with high home values, so a quick sale here usually turns on condition, timing and paperwork rather than on finding demand. The city covers about 33 square miles and sits roughly 22 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. Its 2020 Census population was 83,986, which made it the second-largest community in Oakland County.

Three routes are open to an owner who wants to sell fast: list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase. Each has a different cost in repairs, showings and waiting time. The sections below tie those routes to the rules and numbers that apply inside the city limits.

sections.h2: How did Farmington Hills grow into the city it is now?
sections.html:
The area began as Farmington Township, organized in 1827 after Quaker settlers arrived in the 1820s. The township's remaining land was incorporated as the City of Farmington Hills in 1973, folding in two small villages that had formed in the 1950s, Quakertown and Wood Creek Farms. Growth through the middle of the twentieth century left a mix of postwar subdivisions, condominium communities and larger estate lots.

That history matters to a seller because house age varies a lot from one block to the next. A 1960s colonial and a 1990s estate home sit in the same city but face different buyers and different repair lists.

  • Older subdivisions often need roof, window and furnace updates before a conventional buyer will go forward.
  • Larger estate-style homes draw buyers who expect updated kitchens and finished basements.
  • Condominium sales add association documents and dues to the closing timeline.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Farmington Hills homeowners?
sections.html:
Owners hold most of the housing here, and values sit well above the Michigan cities that share this batch of pages. The figures below come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for the 2020 to 2024 survey period.

The share of residents past 65 is worth noting. Many sellers here are downsizing from a long-held family home, and those homes often carry decades of deferred updates that a buyer will price in.

sections.h2: Which Farmington Hills rules affect a sale or a rental house?
sections.html:
The city runs a mandatory registration and inspection program for single-family rental dwellings. Registered rentals are inspected once every three years, with the review centered on exterior condition, fire safety and egress, structural and electrical items, and sanitation. An owner who is selling a house that has tenants should ask the Planning and Community Development office whether a certificate of compliance is on file and how a transfer to a new owner is handled.

Permits are the other local item. A homeowner may pull permits in place of a licensed contractor only when the person is the registered owner, the home is the primary residence, and the owner lives there. Roofing, siding, window and exterior door replacement, basement finishing and deck work all need a building permit, and water heater, furnace and air conditioner swaps need trade permits. The Building Division can be reached at (248) 871-2450.

  • Fix permit gaps before listing, since a buyer's inspector or lender may ask for proof of finished work.
  • Patios, playground equipment and basketball backboards need no building permit but must meet zoning rules.
  • Residential fence questions go to the Zoning Division at (248) 871-2520.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed in Farmington Hills, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
The city bills a summer tax and a winter tax. The summer bill is mailed June 30 and can be paid from July 1 through August 31 without penalty, then a 4% penalty applies on September 1. The winter bill is mailed November 30 and is due without penalty through mid-February. Unpaid balances move to the Oakland County Treasurer's Office after the last day to pay at City Hall. Treasury answers at 248-871-2480 and Assessing at 248-871-2470.

The city also offers a deferment of summer taxes on a primary residence for owners who are at least 62, totally and permanently disabled, or eligible veterans or surviving spouses, and whose household income falls under a set limit. The 2026 form used a $40,000 income limit. Ask Assessing for the current form if you are still living in the home while selling.

At closing, the title company prorates the current tax bill between seller and buyer. Ask the Treasury office for a payoff or status letter if any prior-year balance might be outstanding.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and filings follow a Farmington Hills sale?
sections.html:
Michigan charges two transfer taxes, and the seller is liable for both. The county tax is 55 cents per $500 of value in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504), and the state tax is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525). The tax is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523).

On a $354,500 sale, the combined $4.30 per $500 works out to roughly $3,050, so that line item is worth budgeting when you compare net proceeds across sale routes. Your title company will show the exact amount on the settlement statement.

The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the city assessor within 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value in the following calendar year (MCL 211.27a), which is why the buyer's tax bill can run well above the seller's.

sections.h2: How do schools, roads and employers shape buyer demand here?
sections.html:
Almost all of the city lies in Farmington Public Schools, while small corners fall in the Clarenceville and Walled Lake districts. North Farmington High School and Farmington Central High School are in the city, and Oakland Community College's Orchard Ridge campus is also here. School district boundaries are one of the first filters buyers apply, so name the district in your listing or your offer conversation.

Commuters value M-5, I-696, I-275, Orchard Lake Road and 12 Mile Road. Major employers named in the city's financial report include Beaumont Hospital, Robert Bosch, Nissan's technical center, Hitachi and Farmington Public Schools. That employer mix keeps a steady pool of relocating professionals looking at the city.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits which Farmington Hills situation?
sections.html:
The right route depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close. A price this high rewards a full renovation and a traditional listing when you have months to spare. It rewards a direct as-is sale when you do not.

  • List with an agent when the home is updated, you can leave it show-ready, and a few months of carrying costs are acceptable.
  • Sell as-is for cash when the house needs a roof, mechanicals or estate cleanout and you want a fixed closing date.
  • Sell to a tenant or investor when the property is a registered rental with a certificate of compliance.

Whichever path you choose, get any offer in writing, compare the net after transfer tax, prorated taxes and any repair credits, and read the closing date terms before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Farmington Hills house that has code problems?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you disclose what you know. A buyer who pays cash can take the house as-is, while a conventional lender may require repairs first. Ask the Building Division at (248) 871-2450 whether open permits exist on the address before you list.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Farmington Hills sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under the state act, though a contract can assign it differently. The county rate is 55 cents and the state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of value, and the county treasurer collects it within 15 days of delivering the deed.

faqs.q: Does a Farmington Hills rental house need an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: The city requires single-family rentals to register and be inspected every three years. If tenants live in the house, ask Planning and Community Development how a sale affects the registration and certificate of compliance.

faqs.q: When are Farmington Hills property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are payable July 1 through August 31 and winter taxes from December 1 to mid-February, with a 4% penalty added after each window. Delinquent bills later move to the Oakland County Treasurer.

faqs.q: How much will my taxes rise for the buyer after the sale?
faqs.a: The buyer's taxable value resets to the state equalized value the year after the transfer, so the new bill can be noticeably higher than yours. The assessor sets the figure, and you can call Assessing at 248-871-2470 for the parcel's current numbers.
